supporting_observations.claim: The alerted HTTPS connections are logged as CONNECT tunnels to update.routewise.com, an approved RouteWise update host in the supplied inventory.

Network and endpoint records associate these connections with C:\Program Files\RouteWise\routewiseupd.exe (PID 6596), the approved RouteWise updater; the observed requests recur at roughly five-minute intervals.

The observed process, destination, and recurring timing are consistent with the inventory description of RouteWise checking update.routewise.com about every five minutes, supporting a benign disposition for the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels, not the encrypted request or response contents.
The supplied records do not include a hash or signature validation for routewiseupd.exe.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the contents or legitimacy of data exchanged inside the HTTPS tunnels.
The evidence does not independently establish that the updater executable was untampered or that the remote endpoint was authentic.
unrelated_findings: At 14:07:45, the host made a separate connection to desktop.dropbox.com using a DropboxUpdate user agent; Dropbox is not an approved service in the supplied inventory. Investigate separately; this does not decide the RouteWise alert. (T136-00254, T136-00255)

Kim Nguyen launched PowerShell, which launched DBeaver and psql with the command line -U postgres -d appdata; database connections to internal addresses 10.52.10.21 and 10.52.10.23 are also recorded. This activity is separate from the alerted RouteWise connections and may merit review. (T136-00032, T136-00034, T136-00035, T136-00063, T136-00107, T136-00111, T136-00114, T136-00118)

The GlobalProtect client was launched on a host in an environment described as having no VPN. The supplied records do not show a VPN connection; investigate the installation or launch separately if unexpected. (T136-00098, T136-00101)
